source: synthetic. Codex's normal chrome while a tool call runs, at the shape a
        real pane shows it: the status line, the tool's own output row beneath
        it, then a blank row, the composer, and the model/cwd footer. The
        elapsed time and the file name are the only invented parts; the row
        order is Codex 0.147's.
why: this is the regression the Phase 2 review found. The status line sits four
     non-empty lines from the bottom, so upstream's `screen_working_fallback`
     (bottom_non_empty_lines(3)) cannot see it, and `sidecar.composer_idle` saw
     the `›` at priority 100 with nothing above it — so a pane in the middle of
     an apply_patch read as a *visible* idle and the tracker announced a
     completed turn mid-turn. The composer rule now carries a `not` gate on the
     interrupt hint and `sidecar.working_chrome` reads twelve lines deep, which
     is what this fixture pins. The title is a plain one on purpose: with a
     spinner in it `osc_title_working` would carry the verdict and the screen
     rules would never be reached.

pane_current_command: codex
pane_height: 24
